newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims up in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims up in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans lining up for first-time unemployment benefits last week rose to its highest level since July, the government reported Thursday.
Filings for state jobless benefits jumped 17,000 to 344,000, the highest level since July 13, when claims stood at 367,000, the Labour Department said in its weekly report.
The gain exceeded forecasts by Wall Street economists, who had predicted that filings would rise only to 332,000.
The previous week's claims were revised downward to 327,000 from 328,000.
The four-week moving average -- viewed as a more reliable economic indicator because it smooths out weekly fluctuations -- jumped 6,250 to 336,250.
The total number of Americans on employment benefit rolls edged up to nearly 2.5 million in the week ended Nov. 9, the most recent period for which that data were available.
The department said eight states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Nov. 9.
California reported the biggest jump, with 3,941 new claims. It attributed the increase to job layoffs in agriculture.
North Carolina, with 2,547 new claims, reported layoffs in the transportation equipment industry.
Other states reporting increases were New York with 2,668, Pennsylvania with 2,016, Michigan with 1,822, Louisiana with 1,697, Minnesota with 1,092 and Washington with 1,060.
New York and Washington provided no explanation for the rise in claims. Pennsylvania reported layoffs in the food, construction and service industries.
Michigan and Louisiana both reported layoffs in the automobile industry. Minnesota reported seasonal layoffs in all industries.
There were no states reporting decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in week ended Nov. 9.
